validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed real, independently of GEM. Three independent outlets in two languages explicitly name this exact segment: (1) Al-Masry Al-Youm (Arabic, the sheet's own current ref, https://www.almasryalyoum.com/news/details/103848) quotes the six-phase breakdown of the South Valley/Upper Egypt trunk and states verbatim 'من بني سويف حتى أبو قرقاص بطول 150كم وقطر 32 بوصة' ('from Beni Suef to Abu Qirqas, length 150km, diameter 32in') -- an exact match to GEM's segment name, length, and diameter; (2) Petroleum Africa ('Mubarak Inaugurates Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline') independently states 'stage two extends 150 km from Beni Suef to Abu Qurqas'; (3) Oil & Gas Journal ('Egypt's Natural Gas Operations and Plans') independently states 'The Beni-Suef/Abu Qorqas line is 150 km (93 miles) of 32 in. with a capacity of 16 MMcfd. It was completed in mid 2007 at a cost of about L.E 545 million.' All three name the same two endpoints and the same 150km/32in figures -- length and diameter are HIGH tier (3 independent sources, exact agreement). CLASSIFICATION: correctly a gas transmission trunk (national grid trunkline supplying residential/industrial/commercial demand across Upper Egypt governorates per Al-Masry Al-Youm), not a gathering/plant-internal line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 30-row Egypt-gas-operating roster and the GulfPub Egypt gas list. GEM's six 'South Valley Gas Pipeline' rows (P6697 Dahshour-Giza, P6698 Al Kurimat-Beni Suef, P6699 Beni Suef-Abu Qurqas, P6700 Abu Qurqas-Asyut, P6701 Asyut-Sohag, P6702 Girga-Aswan) map onto the officially documented six construction phases (Dahshour-Koraimat, Koraimat-Beni Suef, Beni Suef-Abu Qirqas, Abu Qirqas-Asyut, Asyut-Girga/Sohag, Girga-Aswan) and are not duplicates of one another or of P6699. NOTE: GulfPub's own 'South Valley Gas Pipeline' entry for Beni Suef->Abu Qurqus gives len_km=93 (vs. the 150km agreed by 3 independent sources here) -- this looks like a GulfPub geometry/segmentation artifact (it further subdivides the Koraimat-Beni Suef-Abu Qirqas stretch differently than the official phase boundaries), not evidence GEM's 150km is wrong; flagging for awareness, not changing GEM. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co' (EGAS) 100% is corroborated -- Al-Masry Al-Youm names EGAS (Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company) among the entities behind the project; general industry consensus (and GulfPub, cross-checked, not cited) is that EGAS owns the South Valley system while it is operated by a subsidiary ('Nile Valley Gas Company' per GulfPub) / built by Gasco. GEM's gas schema has no separate Operator field for this row (checked live CSV), so there is nothing to fix here -- noting for context only. STATUS: 'operating' is correct; the segment was reportedly complete by mid-2007 and the full six-phase network was ceremonially inaugurated by President Mubarak on 30 Dec 2010 (Egypt Ministry of Petroleum press release date cited on gem.wiki); it has operated continuously since and is unambiguously still in service today.

validity.researcher_notes: GEM's StartYear1=2009 for this segment looks wrong. Oil & Gas Journal states this specific Beni-Suef/Abu Qorqas 150km/32in line 'was completed in mid 2007' (matching cost figure LE 545 million). MEED ('Gasco pipeline on course', published 5 Nov 2006, independently verified) reports construction 'already under way' on the Beni Suef-Abu Qurqas section as of Nov 2006, which is consistent with a mid-2007 completion and inconsistent with a 2009 start. The current sheet ref (almasryalyoum.com/news/details/103848) instead documents the Dec 2010 ceremonial inauguration of the FULL six-phase, 930km South Valley network by President Mubarak -- i.e. the network-wide completion/opening event, not this segment's own in-service date. It looks like GEM applied one project-level start year (2009, close to but still not matching the 2010 inauguration date in its own cited ref) uniformly across all six South Valley segments (P6697-P6702) rather than each phase's individual completion date; this specific segment's own documented completion is 2007. Recommend a human check whether the other five South Valley segments (P6697, P6698, P6700, P6701, P6702) have the same StartYear1=2009 uniformly applied and correct each to its own phase's actual completion year where sourceable -- flagging as a possible class-wide pattern, not fixing the other rows here. Capacity is worth deep-filling here too: OGJ specifically gives 16 MMcfd for this exact segment (GEM's Capacity field is currently blank) -- single strong source, no second independent match found for the segment-specific number (MEED's 24 mcm/d 'design capacity' figure is for the full completed network, not this local spur, so it is not a conflicting figure for this cell, just a different scope), so tier=medium not high; staged as a fill below, not forced.

routes.end_name: Abu Qirqas (Abu Qurqas), Minya Governorate, Egypt
routes.corridor_desc: No named intermediate waypoints were sourced. The line is stage 3 of the six-phase South Valley/Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline, running south from Beni Suef city (Beni Suef Governorate) through the Nile Valley corridor into Minya Governorate, terminating near Abu Qirqas town on the west bank of the Nile (opposite Beni Hasan). Straight-line distance between the two named endpoints is ~130km; the sourced 150km pipe length is consistent with a route roughly paralleling the Nile Valley road/agricultural strip rather than a straight line -- a defensible but loose corridor bound given no waypoints were found. This segment is administratively distinct from the adjacent P6698 (Al Kurimat-Beni Suef, upstream) and P6700 (Abu Qurqas-Asyut, downstream) segments, so the corridor should not be extended past these two named endpoints.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named places in 2 independent sources (OGJ, Petroleum Africa) both explicitly naming 'Beni Suef' and 'Abu Qirqas/Abu Qurqas' as the segment's termini. Coordinates are standard gazetteer coordinates for these two well-known Egyptian towns (Beni Suef city center; Abu Qirqas town center, Minya Governorate), not derived from any route geometry -- no coordinates were fabricated. No intermediate waypoints could be sourced, so the corridor description is bounded by the two named endpoints plus the general Nile Valley routing convention used by the rest of the South Valley trunk (confirmed by RouteNotes on the sheet: 'Nagwa: This is the full route of the pipeline which includes six segments', and RouteType='Included in other ProjectID', meaning the actual route linework for this segment likely already exists bundled under a parent/whole-pipeline ProjectID e.g. P0477 -- a human should check whether that geometry already covers this Beni Suef-Abu Qurqas stretch before drawing anything new).

summary: P6699 (South Valley Gas Pipeline, Beni Suef-Abu Qurqas) confirmed real, correctly classified, no duplicate, attribution OK; StartYear1=2009 is likely wrong (segment-specific completion was mid-2007 per OGJ, contradicting the network-wide 2010 inauguration date the sheet cites) -- flagged as spec concern with a possible class-wide pattern across the other 5 South Valley segments.
